newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Visitors to NZ from Australia up 11 pct in Dec qtr.
newsitem.headline: Visitors to NZ from Australia up 11 pct in Dec qtr.

text.p: Visitor arrivals from Australia increased by 11 percent in the December 1996 quarter over the December 1995 quarter to reach 128,100, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
"Australia was the largest single source with arrivals from there making up 27 percent of all visitors in this period," SNZ said.
The number of visitors from Asia, the second largest source, also rose, increasing by 10 percent on the December 1995 quarter to reach 150,300.
Of the Asian countries, Korea recorded the biggest increase in visitor numbers (5,700), while visitors from China rose by 69 percent to 5,000.

Visitor arrivals from Europe increased by 8.0 percent to 96,700, with United Kingdom visitors accounting for most of the increase. However, a decrease of 2.0 percent was recorded for visitors from North America, with arrivals from the United States dropping by 1,100 to 45,200, but arrivals from Canada increasing slightly.
Overall, overseas visitor arrivals to New Zealand in the December 1996 quarter increased by 9.0 percent over the previous December quarter to reach 479,400, SNZ said.
"There were 277,100 New Zealand resident departures for short trips overseas in the December 1996 quarter, up 32,000 or 13 percent on the previous December quarter," SNZ said.
"Over the same period, departures to Australia rose by 19 percent."
Permanent and long-term migration in the quarter resulted in a net gain of 7,720 migrants, down 24 percent on the net gain of 10,190 in the December 1995 quarter.
There were fewer arrivals from and more departures to Asian countries over the period.
"As a result, the net gain from Asian countries was 3,040 compared with 4,810 in the previous December quarter," SNZ said.
The United Kingdom remained the largest source of net permanent and long-term migrants.
